thread:
Kai: quick note — ran an overnight sweep of KV cache formats across Qwen-34B and Mistral-7B, and we hit a weird perf regression when using BF16 for the prefix cache on Qwen. p95 jumped even though mem dropped.
Mira: do you have the profiler traces? :eyes:
Kai: pasted a trimmed flame: main hotspot is attention_kv_read -> gather_kernels -> fallback_path. Looks like kernel selection picked the generic gather for head_dim=128 which is slower for bf16 on A100.
Jules: is this the RoPE scaling change we rolled last week? could be shifting tiling patterns.
Kai: related — when RoPE scaling increased effective sequence multiplier (we do 1.25x for long contexts), the KV shape changes (seq_len * heads * head_dim) and our kernel chooser ends up selecting a different kernel ID for head_dim=128 vs 64.
Anya: output from the perf-runner:
```
Model: qwen-34b
Config: kv_cache_format=bf16, rope_scale=1.25
p50: 140ms -> 150ms
p95: 210ms -> 285ms   <-- regression
throughput (tokens/s): 420 -> 392
mem(kv): 18.2GB -> 12.6GB
```
Mira: memory win is good but regression is annoying. Did you try FP16 and FP8 quantized cache for comparison?
Kai: FP16 had no regression (p95 212ms) and fp8 (dynamic quant) had slightly higher p95 but similar to BF16. The odd one is BF16 on some kernel paths.
Jules: sounds like a kernel precision path mismatch. Our kernel selector uses heuristics: (head_dim, seq_chunk, dtype) -> kernel_id. We probably only tuned for fp16 before.
Anya: I repro'd locally and captured nvprof slices. The bf16 case uses the general GEMM kernel instead of the small-head optimized GEMM. See snippet:
```
# kernel selection trace
select_kernel(head_dim=128, seq_chunk=64, dtype=bf16) -> kernel_generic_v2
select_kernel(head_dim=128, seq_chunk=64, dtype=fp16) -> kernel_smallhd_opt
```
Kai: proposal: add dtype-aware threshold to chooser and prefer small-head kernels for bf16 if head_dim <= 128 and seq_chunk <= 96. Also add a fallback scoring that accounts for nvcc perf_estimates.
Mira: +1. Also we should update batching heuristics: with bf16 mem lower, autoscaler increased batch depth which increased seq_chunk and pushed kernel choice over threshold. Need to cap batch-induced seq_chunk when using precision variants.
Jules: another angle — eviction policy. Right now it's pure LRU by token count. For quantized caches we should do size-aware LRU (evict biggest kv pages first) and have a quantization-fallback: keep a tiny fp16 working set for hottest prefixes, demote cold prefixes to 4-bit packed.
Kai: sketched config for a new eviction strategy:
```
eviction_policy: size_aware_lru
hot_threshold: 0.02   # top 2% references pinned as fp16
demote_to: int4_packed
prefetch_limit: 3      # limit background prefetch pages
```
Anya: can we simulated-evict to estimate QPS impact? I ran a trace-based simulation; size_aware_lru saved ~1.8GB more than plain LRU and reduced rehydration cloud I/O by 23%.
Mira: important: ensure prefix-cache interactions — when we demote a prefix to int4 we still need to support fast dequant path into the KV gather without blocking the pipeline. That means adding a tiny dequant kernel on the fast path.
Jules: agreed. Also need to add microbench test matrix to CI that exercises combinations: head_dim {64,128,256}, dtype {fp16,bf16,int8}, rope_scale {1.0,1.25,1.5}, seq_chunk {32,64,96}. Currently CI only checks 64/fp16/1.0.
Kai: I'll open a PR with three changes: (1) kernel chooser dtype-aware thresholds + perf scoring, (2) batcher cap for seq_chunk when using low-precision caches, (3) new eviction policy prototype + trace sim. Will attach perf numbers.
perf-bot: scheduled perf sweep for PR #4789 on staging fleet (A100s) — ETA 6h.
Mira: follow-up item — add telemetry: record chosen_kernel_id, head_dim, dtype, seq_chunk in trace logs (low-overhead sample) so field debugging is easier.
Anya: re: RoPE scaling impact — should include an autotune that maps rope_scale -> preferred seq_chunk buckets. Scale can push us into different tiling.
Kai: TL;DR: BF16 is fine for memory but triggers non-optimal kernel for some dims after RoPE scaling + batching. Short-term: enforce small-head kernels for bf16; mid-term: size-aware eviction + quantization tiers; long-term: autotune chooser with perf-model.
Mira: thanks — please drop the PR link and the initial perf artifacts here when ready. :thumbsup:
Kai: will do. ping me if you want the raw nvprof traces.
